bug_report: Two customers escalated this week: one was charged mid-month while still under their plan quota, and another's tiny overage got billed the same as a much larger one - support keeps issuing manual credits and they're eating margin. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix overage_charge so invoices follow the metering policy, without breaking existing behaviour.

conversations.text: Billing escalations again: one customer got charged mid-month and swears they were under their plan quota, another opened a ticket because a 3-unit overrun showed up as a line item at all. Support keeps issuing credits by hand and finance says the credits are eating the margin. Can we make overage_charge actually implement the metering policy instead of whatever it does now?

Right now overage_charge treats the full monthly quota as included from day 1 and bills every unit past it at block_fee/50 per unit. First fix: prorate the included quota by calendar day - allowed so far = plan quota * day_of_month / days_in_month - and I'll truncate that to a whole unit with int(), then bill the units beyond it.

Proration by calendar day is exactly right - quota * day_of_month / days_in_month, that's the policy wording. But do not truncate the fraction. Round UP to the next whole unit, ceil, always: on day 7 of 30 a 1000-unit plan has 233.33 units included, and the customer gets 234. Truncating down is how you charge someone over a rounding artifact, and that's precisely the kind of escalation we're trying to kill.

Ceil it is - the fractional unit counts in the customer's favor. While I'm in meterbill: the worker currently logs nothing when it computes a charge. Want a log line per computed charge so support can trace an invoice without re-deriving it?

One debug-level summary per invoice run with counts, not one line per charge - the metering worker touches every subscription nightly and we already tripped the log-volume alert twice this quarter. Also, unrelated heads-up if you run the suite: the usage-exporter test in this package has been flaky on CI all week - timeouts, not correctness - so rerun before you blame your change.
Noted on both. Back to the charge itself: past the prorated allowance, do we keep billing per unit at block_fee/50? That's what the code does today and it at least makes small overruns cheap.

No - per-unit is the other half of the mess. Overage bills in blocks of 50 units, rounded UP to a whole block: a partial block bills as a full block. 60 units over is two blocks, not 1.2 blocks. The invoice line is blocks times plan['block_fee'], and finance reconciles in whole blocks - per-unit line items are what made reconciliation impossible last quarter.

Whole blocks, always rounded up. Then for the ticket about the 3-unit overrun: under that rule a 3-unit overage still bills one full block. Should I add a minimum threshold - say, waive anything under 10 units - or is the full block intended there?

Neither - there's a piece you haven't been told. After the March billing-support incident we agreed every account gets a grace allowance: the first 25 overage units in a month are free, and the allowance is applied BEFORE the block rounding. So billable = overage minus 25, floored at zero, and only then do you round up into 50-unit blocks. The 3-unit overrun bills nothing, and a 60-unit overage bills 35 billable units, which is one block - not two.

So the order of operations is fixed: ceil-prorated allowance first, subtract the 25-unit grace from the overage, then round what's left up into 50-unit blocks and multiply by block_fee. If I flipped grace and blocking - rounding to blocks first, then knocking 25 units off - I'd get different invoices.

Exactly, and that flipped order is wrong - the sequence is prorate with ceil, then grace, then blocks. It's the difference between the 60-unit case billing one block or two, and support has been crediting exactly that difference by hand.
Understood. Different topic before I forget - rollout. This changes real invoice amounts; do you want the new computation behind a billing feature flag with a comparison period, or shipped directly?

No flag - billing flags never get cleaned up and then nobody knows which formula produced an invoice. Stage it the usual way: internal tenants for one nightly run, diff the generated invoices against the policy spreadsheet, then everyone. Support already has the macro update queued.

Will do. Two boundary checks so the tests are right: on the last day of the month the prorated allowance should equal the full quota, and usage exactly at the prorated allowance is not overage at all, correct?

Correct on both - day 30 of 30 includes the whole quota, and usage at or under the allowance owes nothing. The plan dict carries 'quota' and 'block_fee'; keep the ValueError for a day outside 1..days_in_month, that guard has caught real caller bugs.

Final recap of overage_charge: validate day_of_month is within 1..days_in_month; included allowance = plan quota * day_of_month / days_in_month rounded UP to the next whole unit (ceil, never truncation); overage = usage beyond that allowance; the first 25 overage units in the month are the free grace allowance, applied BEFORE block rounding; the remainder bills in 50-unit blocks rounded UP so a partial block bills as a full block, at plan['block_fee'] per block - never per unit. Prorate with ceil, then grace, then blocks.

policy: included quota prorates by calendar day (quota * day_of_month / days_in_month, rounded UP to the next whole unit); first 25 overage units per month are a free grace allowance applied BEFORE block rounding; the remainder bills in 50-unit blocks rounded UP (partial block = full block) at plan['block_fee'] per block, never per unit
